transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?

I’m here because my talking gets all mixed up. I’ll start trying to explain something about the keys, then I’m on the jail, then the prayer rug or chess pieces, and people tell me they can’t follow what I’m saying.
How long have you been noticing this problem with your thoughts and talking getting mixed up?
About two years and five months now. It started after that brief detention over the misunderstanding at the building.
During these past two years, have you had periods lasting weeks where you felt deeply depressed or down?
Yeah. On my bad days, after morning prayer, I just sit on the edge of the bed feeling heavy and empty. It feels like there’s no point even cleaning myself up or going outside.
Have you had this trouble with your thoughts and speech even during times when you were not feeling depressed?
Yes. Even when I’m not feeling down, my words still get mixed up. I’ll be talking about the keys, then I end up on the jail, the prayer rug, or chess pieces, and people can’t follow me.
Looking back over these past two and a half years, would you say you felt that depressed for most of that time, or only for a small part of it?
Only part of it. Altogether, those heavy, hopeless stretches add up to about seven months, not most of the two and a half years.
